findings.title: The Region B recommendation depends on a demand figure with no source.
findings.principle: Evidence Grounding: a claim that drives a decision must be sourced.
findings.diagnosis: The case for Region B on slides 7 to 9 rests on the demand growth stated on slide 5. That figure carries no source, no baseline and no method, so the recommendation is currently unsupported.

evidence.quote: Region B demand will grow 40% over the next three years.

findings.why: A partner or funder who asks where the number comes from gets no answer, and the whole expansion case falls with it.
findings.reflect: Where does the 40% come from, and what would you accept as a credible source for it.
findings.fix: Source the demand estimate or replace it with a range you can defend, then show the recommendation still holds. If you cannot source it, mark it as an assumption and test whether the recommendation survives without it.

findings.title: The recommendation names no action, owner, timeframe or metric.
findings.principle: Actionability: a recommendation names the action, the owner, the timing and the measure.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 9 tells Client A to scale up operations and improve partnerships. Neither phrase says what to do first, who owns it or how success is measured.

evidence.quote: Scale up operations and improve partnerships to serve the new region.

findings.why: A one-coordinator team cannot act on a direction. It needs a first step and a way to know the step worked.
findings.reflect: If you were the coordinator on Monday morning, what is the first concrete thing you would do, and how would you know it worked.
findings.fix: Turn the recommendation into a sequenced first step with an owner and a success signal, sized to a one-coordinator team. Keep it to what they can actually resource.

findings.title: The governing insight appears on slide 8 and the titles are topic labels.
findings.principle: Pyramid Principle: answer first, and titles carry the message.
findings.diagnosis: The view that Region B is the priority first appears on slide 8. Titles such as Agenda and Our view are labels, so a reader skimming the titles cannot follow the argument.

evidence.quote: Client A should prioritize Region B.
Context. Current operations. Regional demand. Options. Recommendation. Next steps.

findings.why: A busy funder reading only the titles cannot see the recommendation or why it holds, so the argument does not land.
findings.reflect: If a reader saw only your slide titles, could they state your recommendation and one reason for it.
findings.fix: Move the governing insight to the front and rewrite the content titles as full-sentence assertions so the titles alone carry the argument.

comments.problem: Next steps are not time-bound ("Review progress in due course").
comments.why: A vague timeline means no one is accountable for momentum.
comments.fix: Give the first two steps an owner and a date.

comments.why: The size of unmet demand in Region A is the counterweight to the Region B case, so it needs a number.
comments.fix: Quantify the unmet demand if the data exists, or mark it as an estimate.

questionsForLead: Where did the 40% Region B demand figure come from, and did anyone verify it.
Did the team ask Client A whether it has the funding and staff to open a Region B hub, or is that assumed.
Has the team quantified the unmet demand in Region A so the two options can be compared on the same basis.
What would success look like in the first year of whichever option is chosen.

learningNote.lesson: A recommendation is only as strong as the number it rests on. When one figure carries the decision, sourcing it is not optional.
learningNote.weakHabit: Reaching a confident recommendation before the evidence under it is nailed down.
learningNote.exercise: Take the recommendation and list every claim it depends on. For each, write the source. Any claim with no source is the next thing to go and get.
